headline: 30-day ban for Ronaldo: Portugal suspends Cristiano Ronaldo over camp walkout
summary: The Portuguese FA has fined the Al-Nassr star £215 and issued a month-long suspension following a fallout with head coach Jorge Jesus.
details: Cristiano Ronaldo has been handed a 30-day suspension and a £215 fine by the Portuguese FA’s disciplinary council. The penalty follows his abrupt departure from the national team camp in Copenhagen earlier this month.

The incident occurred on October 2, when Ronaldo left the squad on the eve of a Nations League match against Denmark. This followed a dispute with head coach Jorge Jesus after Ronaldo was an unused substitute against Norway and was omitted from the starting lineup against Denmark.

Ronaldo accused coach Jesus of an "absolute breach of trust" in an open letter on social media, claiming the manager had broken his word regarding his role. Coach Jesus has firmly denied these allegations.

Despite the conflict, Ronaldo has since apologized for abandoning his teammates and fans, stating that he deserves the punishment. He has confirmed that he is not retiring from international football as he aims for 1,000 career goals.

The Portuguese FA and coach Jorge Jesus have both expressed their desire to welcome him back once the suspension is served. Portugal is scheduled to play Denmark again on November 14 in the Nations League.
Ronaldo remains the most capped player and highest international goalscorer in history, with 146 goals and 234 appearances for Portugal.

headline_marked: Lawmaker Ishraque Hossain [[resigns as state minister]] after firearm controversy
headline: Lawmaker Ishraque Hossain resigns as state minister after firearm controversy
summary: The Dhaka-6 MP stepped down following backlash over a video showing him brandishing a pistol during an anti-drug drive in Gendaria.
details: Dhaka-6 lawmaker Ishraque Hossain has resigned from the council of ministers. He served as the state minister for Liberation War Affairs.
The resignation follows a controversy involving an 'anti-drug drive' in Gendaria, where Ishraque was seen in a video brandishing a firearm.
Other footage from the operation showed people accompanying him carrying guns, with one person threatening to shoot and a bodyguard kicking a young man.
Ishraque defended the operation, stating it was coordinated with local law enforcement and aimed at dismantling drug networks. He claimed six people were handed over to police.
During a press briefing, he stated he voluntarily expressed his intention to quit to focus more on public activities and anti-drug campaigns in his constituency.
He maintained that he had acted properly and carried the firearm for his protection, noting that he has two registered firearms in his name.
The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has ordered an investigation into the incident, as the Firearms Policy 2025 bars the display of weapons in ways that cause fear or annoyance.
Ishraque also expressed his readiness to contest the Dhaka mayoral election if nominated by his party and chairman.
